title:
The "model" encapsulates data access methods needed by a user interface to interact with the underlying data of a
single logical object in some data repository. This may end up devolving into multiple related objects, perhaps
even in different underlying data stores.

A model maintains state locally about changes made which have not yet been saved to the server. The #set method
changes data locally (applying simple validation), but does not send anything to the server and just marks the
local model as dirty. When #save is called, all pending changes are bundled up and submitted to the server in a
single request and if the server responds with a success status, the model becomes clean.

Models support these {@link UiEventSource events}:
 - `change`: a change to one or more fields of the model
 - `save`: the model was successfully saved to the server
 - `reload`: the model instance was reloaded from the server

The model only manages the data of an object. The presentation is configured using a {@link UiView view}.

It also doesn't act as a controller, that is done by defining a {@link ReactComponent component}. For example,
{@link ModelForm} is a generic controller component for models that presents the contents as a form.

Methods which delegate processing to the server are asynchronous and return a Promise.

@see UiCollection
@see UiView
